summary: Iter44 Home page filter overhaul tested end-to-end. Backend: 18/19 tests pass in new test_iter44.py; 42/42 regression tests (iter40+41+42+43) still pass. Frontend: all 9 acceptance criteria verified via Playwright — search input + clear, category-aware secondary filter switching (Healthcare→specialization / Automobile→service), city typeahead with dropdown + Mumbai suggestion click, clear-all button, combined q+city surfaces TestHospital via sub-doctor union match, and empty-state text is exact. One minor spec deviation: Automobile /reference/filters returns 7 options (not 8) — the frontend dropdown renders 8 items only because it prepends the label as a placeholder option. Actual selectable services = 7.

minor.issue: Spec says 8 vehicle-service options, backend returns only 7: ['Car Wash','Full Detailing','Oil Change','Tyre Service','Denting & Painting','General Service','AC Service']. Missing 8th option (candidate: 'Battery Service' or similar) — see server.py _CATEGORY_FILTERS['automobile']['options'].

action_items: Add the 8th Automobile service option in /app/backend/server.py _CATEGORY_FILTERS['automobile']['options'] to match spec (current list has 7).
critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/server.py is now 3287 lines — well past the 700-line guideline. Recommend splitting reference/search/booking domains into modules (e.g. routers/reference.py, routers/search.py).

/reference/cities uses `{'$regex': f'^{q}'}` without escaping user input — a client sending `q='.*'` or regex metachars will still work but a malformed regex like `q='['` could raise. Consider re.escape(q) before injecting into the regex.
/search/providers builds a Mongo `$or` clause from user input `q` via unescaped regex — same regex-injection surface. Low risk (no DoS pathway visible) but worth escaping.

Home.jsx effect deps include `filterSpec.param` — because filterSpec is replaced on each category change, this triggers an extra debounced /search/providers call right after the category change. Harmless but wasteful; consider consolidating.

success_rate.backend: 94.7% (18/19 iter44 tests, 100% regression on 42 prior tests)
